events.title: Fire Ranger Competition
events.description: **Event Title:** 🔥 Fire Ranger Challenge 🔥 **Event Type:** Troop Meeting / Skills Competition **Date:** Tuesday, November 4th, 2025 **Time:** 6:00 PM - 8:00 PM **Location:** Living Word Baptist Church, Sweet Valley, PA ----- **Event Description:** Join us for THE FIRE RANGER CHALLENGE—an epic evening where Trailmen will compete in fire-building skills, practice servant leadership, and master critical fire safety techniques! **Navigators & Adventurers** will compete head-to-head building fires (Teepee or Log Cabin), boiling water for hot chocolate, and roasting the perfect marshmallow for s’mores. First to deliver hot chocolate AND a perfect s’more to Troopmaster Chris wins! **Mountain Lions** serve as “gophers,” delivering supplies and demonstrating servant leadership by ensuring fires are never left unattended. **Hawks & Foxes** learn fire safety through our new game SPARK, SPARK, FIRE! (Stop, Drop, and Roll training), then man the hot chocolate and s’more stations. **Skills Covered:** - Fire building (tinder, kindling, fuel wood) - Teepee and Log Cabin fire lays - Safe match striking - Fire tending and maintenance - Proper fire extinguishing (DEAD OUT!) - Stop, Drop, and Roll - Servant leadership **Spiritual Focus:** *“For our God is a consuming fire.”* - Hebrews 12:29 (KJV) Boys will learn how fire appears throughout Scripture (burning bush, Elijah calling down fire, pillar of fire) and practice being good stewards of God’s creation. ----- **What to Bring:** **All Trailmen:** - Trail Life uniform - Weather-appropriate clothing (cotton/wool, NO synthetics) - Closed-toe shoes (NO flip-flops) - Water bottle **Navigators & Adventurers ONLY:** - Special chocolate for s’mores (Reese’s, York Peppermint Patty, etc.) **NOTE:** Pots provided! ----- **Safety Notes:** - All fires supervised by trained adults - Proper safety equipment on-site - Weather monitored (may reschedule if unsafe) - Strict safety protocols enforced **Special Notes:** Hot chocolate and s’mores for everyone! Come ready to compete, serve, and learn. Building fires AND building men of God! 🔥✝️ *As iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.* - Proverbs 27:17 (KJV)

events.title: Men at Work
events.description: Men at Work is a powerful weekend experience for any man involved in Trail Life. Hosted at Camp Aiken in South Carolina, this event combines the most impactful elements of Equip 64, past Equip events, and the Gathering of Worthy Trailmen to deliver practical training, outdoor skill-building, and authentic brotherhood. Men will camp in patrols, share meals together, learn from Trail Life subject matter experts, dig deep in devotionals, and enjoy meaningful fireside conversations. With built-in time to reflect, recharge, and reconnect, Men at Work is designed to equip and inspire men to lead with courage and confidence—on the trail, in their homes, and in every aspect of life. Register Today!

events.title: Big Horn National Forest Hike
events.description: In the summer of 2026, the Central Virginia Trail Life High Adventure Team is planning an extraordinary high adventure trek. This year we will be hiking the trails of the Big Horn National Forest / Cloud Peak Wilderness in Wyoming. Our proposed route will cover 90 miles and will include a day hike to the summit of Cloud Peak, at elevation 13,000 feet. In years past, we have hiked the Appalachian Trail through the Shenandoah National Park (120 miles), rode our bikes along the Great Allegheny Passage and C&O Canal Towpath (320 miles), participated in a Missions Trip to Kyrgyzstan with hiking in the Altyn Arashan valley, canoed the Northern Forest Canoe Trail in central New York (60 miles), and have now decided it is time to experience some scenery different from our East Coast world. The dates for this high adventure will be August 3 rd through August 14 th of 2026. Adventurers and Navigators who are 14 or have completed the 8th grade are invited to participate. Space will be limited to 10 Trailmen and 5 adults. If the number of Trailmen is less than 10, more adults are welcome to join the team. Expression of early interest is important to secure your spot in the team. Our team leaders will be Frank Corwin, member of VA-1807, experienced hiker and High Adventure Coordinator for Central Virginia and Blade Alexander, Freedom Rangeman and member of VA-4034. In addition, we will be partnering with Trail Life Troop WY-3078 in Wyoming, who will provide ground support and join us for segments of the trail. The cost of the trek has not been finalized yet, but we plan to keep it at $1200 or less per team member. Each hiker will receive a custom jersey to wear on the trek and to remember it by. Costs will include all transportation, food and camping fees. There are online planning meetings currently happening for all those interested in attending. The link code for these meetings will be sent to everyone who is interested. In preparation for this adventure, we will host at least two weekend shake-down hikes that all team members would need to attend. These hikes will be local in Virginia and on the Appalachian Trail. Each hike will cover at least 20 to 30 miles. Proposed schedule, menu, personnel and crew packing lists and a recommended exercise plan will be shared during our planning meetings. Trailmen may have the opportunity to earn various Freedom Experiences during the trek, such as: EXP 201: Backpacking Wilderness Trip EXP 401: Mountaineering SURV 201: Wilderness Preparation. If you are interested or have questions about this High Adventure Opportunity, please RSVP to Frank, at fdc1807@gmail.com .

events.title: Nerfaggedon: Gettysburg Campaign Weekend
events.description: Step back to July 1863 and experience a weekend of strategy, leadership, teamwork, and high-energy Nerf competition inspired by the historic Battle of Gettysburg . This is not just a foam dart free-for-all. This is structured, mission-driven, patrol-based engagement rooted in history and Trail Life values. Trailmen will: Reenact key phases of Gettysburg in scenario-based battles Earn ammunition through skill-based patrol stations Operate within chain of command and rank structure Compete with honor, discipline, and brotherhood The weekend emphasizes courage, leadership, preparedness, and teamwork — the same traits demonstrated by soldiers who fought at Gettysburg. Each Troop will be responsible for their own food for the weekend and must bring their own Potable water as there is no running water on site. It will be up to each troop to decide if they invite their foxes and hawks. Stations will be geared towards Mt. Lions and above. We will break up troops and create new patrols with members from different troops. Featured Battle Scenarios McPherson Ridge – First Contact Cemetery Hill – Hold the High Ground Little Round Top – Stand Fast Devil’s Den – Close Quarters Engagement The Peach Orchard – The Overextended Line Pickett’s Charge – The Long Walk Cemetery Ridge – Final Engagement Each scenario includes a historical briefing to help Trailmen understand what took place and why it mattered. Ammo Earning Stations Before battle, patrols must earn their ammunition by completing skill-based challenges including: Fire building Wilderness first aid Map & compass navigation Lashings & field engineering Physical fitness challenge Communication relay Trail cooking Leadership decision scenarios Marksmanship challenge Gear inspection & readiness No skill. No ammo. Simple as that. What to Bring Nerf blaster (no modified or high-velocity blasters) Eye protection (mandatory at all times during battles) Full field uniform Camping gear (TL packing list) Water bottle & hydration system Positive attitude and willingness to lead Safety & Structure Strict eye protection policy Clear battle boundaries Adult supervision at all battle stations Defined medic rules Chain of command enforced Christ-centered leadership throughout the weekend Schedule Snapshot Friday Check-in & campsite setup Opening assembly & historical briefing Campfire and movie Saturday Morning skill stations (earn ammo) Afternoon battle scenarios Evening campfire reflection Sunday Devotional & closing ceremony Break camp

events.title: National Day of Prayer
events.description: National Day of Prayer . This is a nationally-organized event held annually on the 1st Thursday in May. Each year has a Scriptural theme/verse. Secular communities come together for non-sectarian prayer for local, state, and national leaders—in government, education, military, first responders, etc. Usually organized by city governments or churches. Emphasis : Keeps prayer in the forefront in cities and towns; allows Trail Life Troops to serve (set-up, ushers, flag presentation, etc). National Day of Prayer Website
